html:
A poet of the Tang dynasty in China, who wrote about war, hunger, ruined families and the duty of officials. With his friend Li Bai he is counted among the two greatest Chinese poets.

He hoped for a career in government but failed the examinations and held only minor posts. In 755 the An Lushan Rebellion tore the empire apart. Du Fu was caught in the occupied capital, escaped, and spent his later years moving with his family from place to place, often poor. For a few years he lived in a thatched cottage at Chengdu in Sichuan. He died on a boat in Hunan in 770.

His poem "Spring View", written in captured Chang'an, opens: "The nation is broken, but hills and rivers remain." Little known in his lifetime, he was later called the "poet sage". Li Bai is the free spirit; Du Fu is the poet of conscience and careful craft, a master of the strict eight-line form.
sum: A poet of the Tang dynasty in China, who wrote about war, hunger, ruined families and the duty of officials. With his friend Li Bai he is counted among the two greatest Chinese poets.
